gates.title: Popularity, installed base, prices, and real VB applications
gates.scope_in_this_asset: The image must be a real application with documented classic-VB provenance, and the artwork must carry no statistics or rankings.

checks.claim: The depicted application was built in classic Visual Basic.
checks.evidence: The publisher's own 1993 documents in the archived distribution: RELEASE.TXT v2.00 (02/17/93) 'Recompiled program using Visual BASIC 2.0'; HELP.TXT and MANUAL.WRI 'The program is now running under Visual BASIC version 2.0'; the MANUAL.WRI installation section requires 'the Visual BASIC runtime library, VBRUN200.DLL'. This is an explicit vendor statement plus a runtime requirement, not an inference from gray controls.

checks.claim: The depicted application is a business tool (the script's 'internal business tools').
checks.evidence: HELP.TXT: designed for creating and printing invoices; integrates with the publisher's 'Total Business Solution' accounting software. The screenshot shows the invoice form (File #, Salesman, PO #, Qty/Reference/Description/Cost/Extended, SUBTOTAL).

checks.claim: Era and version of the depicted program.
checks.evidence: The distribution is dated 1993-06-12/13 and its latest release note is 2.06 (06/12/93). The screen itself was captured on 2016-02-27 in emulation, and the on-screen Date field shows 02-27-2016. That field is left visible, not cropped. Any caption must not call the image a 1993 photograph of the screen.

checks.claim: No statistics, rankings, or prices are added to the artwork.
checks.evidence: The editorial frame adds no text. The screen's own sample values (invoice number 3379, sales form labels) come from the program's default data.

checks.claim: Narration (SCRIPT.md:685): accountants wrote spreadsheet tools, teachers built quiz apps, small business owners made inventory trackers, and similar broad assertions about who used VB.
checks.evidence: This asset documents one small-vendor VB invoicing product. That fits the paragraph's theme but does not prove its generalizations. It was made by a software publisher, not by a business owner automating their own work. Per R11 the broad narration is routed to the producer.

gates.reason: The application-level VB provenance is documented. The broad narration assertions are outside what this asset can prove, so they go to review, not self-clearance.
review_questions: R11 narration: SCRIPT.md:685 generalizes about accountants, teachers and small business owners. XTRA-11 documents only one real example: INVOICE-IT for Windows, a 1993 VB 2.0 invoicing shareware by a small publisher. Keep the narration as illustrative color, or soften it (for example to 'small businesses got invoicing and inventory tools')? If wording changes, the Writing Lead owns War/SCRIPT.md.

gates.title: Per-image licensing, archive capture, and public availability

checks.claim: Rights holder, file-specific terms, access method, and credit are recorded.
checks.evidence: Rights holders: Eastern Digital Resources (software/UI), plus the Internet Archive Software Library capture. The item has no license field and no rights statement. The publisher's shareware terms cover redistributing the trial software, not images. Access was a public anonymous download with no account, terms, CAPTCHA, or payment.

checks.claim: The image is licensed for use in the video.
checks.evidence: No license, public-domain dedication, or permission found. Public availability on archive.org is not a license.

checks.claim: No private or sensitive personal data is visible.
checks.evidence: The screen shows an empty invoice form with program defaults only: no customer names, addresses, or contact details. The publisher's contact details from the documents were not copied into the asset or the excerpts.

gates.reason: Rights are unclear. Release stays blocked until the review deck decides on use (fair-use rationale or permission) or cuts the image.
review_questions: R14 rights: may the video show this Internet Archive emulator screenshot of 1993 shareware (INVOICE-IT for Windows, Eastern Digital Resources; item MEDLEY_SEC90034, no license on file) as a brief collage element with credit, on a fair-use or commentary rationale? Or should permission be sought, or the image cut?
